newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Pioneer Hi-Bred cut.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Pioneer Hi-Bred cut.

text.p: -- Dain Bosworth analyst Bonnie Wittenburg said Friday she had cut her rating on seed company Pioneer Hi-Bred International Inc to hold from buy based on price.
-- Wittenburg reiterated her buy ratings on seed company DeKalb Genetics Corp and agricultural companies Monsanto Co and Mycogen Corp.

-- She said she believes valuations for strategic segments of the seed industry could be heightened by the anticipated sale of Holden Foundation Seeds. She said Monsanto is seen as the most likely buyer of Holden.
-- A Monsanto spokeswoman declined comment on the speculation. Holden officials were not available for comment.

-- In a report, Wittenburg, quoting "various sources in the seed industry," said Holden was expected to announce soon that it was being sold to Monsanto. She said the potential purchase price could be more than $900 million.

-- "The price for Holden, which would represent a huge multiple on Holden's estimated sales of $35 million and estimated annual profit of $5-$10 million, could be expected to heighten valuations for strategic segments of the seed industry," Wittenburg wrote.
-- She said the downgrade of Pioneer was due to price, not fundamentals.

-- "Further, we believe that the stock market will view a Monsanto-Holden combination as more viable competition for Pioneer," she said. "Seed company valuations are rising with all of the consolidation and technology frenzy, but we expect the market to pay more attention to the stocks of DeKalb, Mycogen and Monsanto than Pioneer."
-- Pioneer was down 3/8 at 70-3/8. Monsanto was up 7/8 at 39-5/8, Mycogen was up 1/2 at 22-1/4, and DeKalb was up 1-5/8 at 51-1/8.
